[quote=united_hydronia;59551276][b]Vacan Diplomacy - Arrival in Hydropolis[/b]
On the crisp morning of May 25th, a plane arrives at Hydropolis Airport. The plane carries representatives from the Democratic Republic of Vacan. As the plane touches down, President Zorlu and the minister of foreign affairs, Halis Erdemir wait eagerly. Both men extend their hands to the Vacan diplomats as they exit the aircraft.
[i]Welcome to Hydronia![/i]

[nation]Vacan[/nation][/quote]
A sleek VA-3C jet bearing the Vacani coat of arms, showing a brown bear poised under a seven-spoked star, taxied to a halt at Hydropolis International Airport at 08:44 local time. The door opened slowly to the early morning sun, revealing the official delegation. At the front stood Minister of Foreign Affairs Lerna Halvek, a sharp-tongued technocrat known for her pragmatism and deep ties to Vacans industrial lobby. Beside her, Dr. Kevar Dastin, Undersecretary for Trade and Innovation, carried a sealed portfolio. Accompanying them were two senior advisors from the Ministry of Commerce and an attaché from the newly formed Office for External Science Partnerships.
As Lerna Halvek descended, she extended her hand first to Zorlu, then to Erdemir.
President Zorlu, Minister Erdemir, she said on behalf of President Anton Rayne and the Vacani people, we thank you for this opportunity. We are here to build something long lasting together with you.

The president smiled, then said,
[i]"I'd like to thank you, for giving us another opportunity for establishing diplomatic ties. There's nothing I enjoy more than creating good relations with nations like yours! Now, if you'll follow us, we have a taxi waiting to take us to the old Imperial Conference hall,"[/i]

[b]Baladullah to Host Regional Interfaith Peace and Dialogue Conference in Medinah al-Islam from 1-3 Muharram(July 4-6)[/b]

[u]Al-Naba News Service | 4 Dhul-Hijjah 1446
[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [/i]

Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi announced today that Baladullah will be hosting a conference on interfaith dialogue and peace building next month. It is open to all religious leaders in the entire region, and will feature panels and discussions on the similarities between religious morals and ethics, Q & A sessions hosted by leaders of Sunni Islam, Shia Islam, Druzism, Judaism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism, and group activities for people of different faiths to learn about one anothers religious backgrounds and practices.

So far, all the top religious leaders of the different faiths in Baladullah (Sunni Islam, Shia Islam, Orthodox Judaism, Orthodox Christianity, Druzism, and Zoroastrianism) have stated their intentions to attend.

Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi cordially extends an invitation to all religious leaders in all countries in the region to attend. In shaa Allah, this can be a positive step towards genuine peace, cooperation, and goodwill between all religions.
